title: M3-A9 — Daltonized colorBlindMode: remap the whole semantic color set, not just toolDiffAdded
one_line: Today colorBlindMode recolors exactly one token (the green in added-diff lines); this widens it to the five semantic green/red/amber tokens that actually collide for a red-green colorblind reader, remapping each to a distinct target hue band, and adds a contrast regression harness that checks every builtin theme instead of eyeballing one.
user_visible_effect: With Color-Blind Mode on, a red-green colorblind reader can now tell added-diff lines apart from success ticks, from a clean git status, and from an error — today only added-diff lines change, so `success` and `statusLineGitClean` stay green and still read as 'added line' at a glance. Every theme keeps its own character because the remap carries each palette's own lightness and chroma, so `titanium` stays as muted as it was. With Color-Blind Mode off nothing changes at all, byte for byte. The setting's description in the Appearance tab becomes honest about covering more than diffs.
effort: S (~1 day). The plan's M variant (~5 days) was justified by 'you must audit 99 palettes first' — that audit is DONE below and comes back clean, which removes the stated blocker for the S variant. Remaining M-only work is two hand-tuned themes, which is design parity with the reference, not a correctness fix; see open_questions.
risk: Applying one uniform hue delta to five tokens collides them. Red is h=0; the existing +60 delta sends it to h=60 (yellow), which is exactly where `statusLineGitDirty` already lives — so a naive 'add error, success, statusLineGitClean, statusLineGitDirty to the same branch' patch would make error and dirty-git render the same color, a regression that is invisible in review and obvious to the user it was meant to help. This is precisely the failure the plan says the reference avoids by shipping two hand-tuned themes. The fix is to remap each token to a distinct TARGET hue band, not to add one more token to a fixed delta.

plan_corrections.claim: `statusLineGitClean`/`statusLineGitDirty` are declared at `packages/tui/src/theme/schema.ts:77-78` 'with a fallback at :140-141', so a missing key would silently skip the adjustment.
plan_corrections.correction: The line numbers are right, but :140-141 is NOT a fallback. Both lines sit inside `THEME_COLOR_RECORD` (schema.ts:89), which exists only to build `VALID_THEME_COLORS` (schema.ts:152) for `isValidThemeColor` (schema.ts:156). It is a validation allowlist, not a default-color layer. There is no default-filling layer anywhere: `resolveThemeColors` (color.ts:64-73) iterates only keys present in the palette, and `theme-class.ts:167-169` drops any key failing `isValidThemeColor` via `continue`. A missing key therefore yields an ABSENT color, not a fallback color — so the implementer must not expect a missing key to render as something reasonable.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -n THEME_COLOR_RECORD -- packages/tui/src` → only two hits: schema.ts:89 (definition) and schema.ts:152 (`const VALID_THEME_COLOR_RECORD = new Set(...)` → VALID_THEME_COLORS). `sed -n '64,73p' packages/tui/src/theme/color.ts` shows `resolveThemeColors` looping `Object.entries(colors)` only. `sed -n '167,169p' packages/tui/src/theme/theme-class.ts` → `if (!isValidThemeColor(key)) continue;`.

plan_corrections.claim: The small patch 'must come with a 99-palette inventory checking each key exists and is a hex string' because 'a missing or non-hex key silently ignores the adjustment'.
plan_corrections.verdict: VERIFIED TRUE, AND THE AUDIT IS NOW DONE — it comes back clean
plan_corrections.correction: I ran the inventory the plan demanded. All 99 palettes in `packages/tui/src/theme/defaults/` contain `toolDiffAdded`, `success`, `error`, `statusLineGitClean`, and `statusLineGitDirty`. None is missing, so no key is silently skipped. One nuance the plan misses: the raw JSON is mostly `var:` indirection, not literal hex — e.g. onyx.json has `"toolDiffAdded": "$emerald"` with `vars.emerald = "#6fb37f"`. `resolveVarRefs` (color.ts:49-62) resolves those at `resolveThemeColors`, which runs at loader.ts:151 BEFORE the colorBlindMode branch reads them at :153. So the branch always sees resolved hex and the existing `startsWith("#")` guard holds on all 99. The silent-skip risk is therefore real only for a 256-color number or `""` value, which can come from a user-authored custom theme, not a builtin.
plan_corrections.evidence: Script over `packages/tui/src/theme/defaults/*.json` asserting all four keys present: output is a single line `99 True`. `sed -n '16p;23p;51p;74p' packages/tui/src/theme/defaults/onyx.json` → `"emerald": "#6fb37f"`, `"success": "$emerald"`, `"toolDiffAdded": "$emerald"`, `"statusLineGitClean": "$emerald"`. `ls packages/tui/src/theme/defaults/*.json | wc -l` → 99.

plan_corrections.claim: The regression harness should run across 'all 99 palettes'.
plan_corrections.correction: `BUILTIN_THEMES` (loader.ts:18-22) is `dark.json` + `light.json` + the 99 `defaults/*.json`, i.e. 101 themes. `dark` and `light` are the two the app actually boots with when no theme is configured, and they are not in the defaults directory. A harness that globs `defaults/*.json` misses exactly the two themes most users see. Iterate `getBuiltinThemes()` (loader.ts:24) instead, which is the same map the picker uses.
plan_corrections.evidence: `sed -n '18,26p' packages/tui/src/theme/loader.ts` → `const BUILTIN_THEMES: Record<string, ThemeJson> = { dark: darkThemeJson, light: lightThemeJson, ...(defaultThemes as Record<string, ThemeJson>) };` followed by `export function getBuiltinThemes() { return BUILTIN_THEMES; }`.

plan_corrections.claim: The new themes are 'selectable from ThemePicker like any normal theme'.
plan_corrections.verdict: STALE — no ThemePicker exists in this repo
plan_corrections.correction: `git grep -rn 'ThemePicker|theme-picker' -- packages/` returns nothing. Theme selection is `setTheme` / `previewTheme` (theme.ts:211 / :248) driven by `getAvailableThemes` (loader.ts:29) and the `cfgThemeDark` / `cfgThemeLight` settings (settings.ts:58). A theme is 'just a theme' when it is imported in `packages/tui/src/theme/defaults/index.ts` and added to the `defaultThemes` object literal — that is the whole registration cost, and it needs no picker change. This matters only for the M variant, which is why the S variant below touches no UI file at all.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -rn 'ThemePicker|theme-picker' -- packages/ | grep -v test` → empty. `tail -15 packages/tui/src/theme/defaults/index.ts` shows the object literal keyed by theme name (`titanium: titanium,`).

plan_corrections.verdict: RIGHT AREA, WRONG LINE AND INCOMPLETE — there are four consumer sites, not one
plan_corrections.correction: settings.ts:109-120 is the declaration: `export const cfgColorBlindMode = register({ id: "colorBlindMode" ... })` with `id` at :110 and `effect(cfgColorBlindMode, setColorBlindMode)` at :120. Line 108 is the blank line above it. But the actual hand-off into `createTheme` is at `main.ts:1909` via `applyStartupComposerPreferences({ theme: { colorBlindMode: cfgColorBlindMode.get(settingsInstance) } })`, and there are two more consumers: `modes/setup.ts:90-92` and `cli/gallery-cli.ts:29` / `commands/git.ts:13`. A reader who follows only settings.ts:108 will not find the wiring to the TUI.
plan_corrections.evidence: `sed -n '1907,1912p' packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts` → `colorBlindMode: cfgColorBlindMode.get(settingsInstance),` inside the `theme: {` object. `sed -n '90,92p' packages/coding-agent/src/modes/setup.ts` → `get colorBlindMode() { return cfgColorBlindMode.get(ctx.settings); }`.

plan_corrections.claim: OKLCH primitives `hexToOklch, oklchCusp, oklchToHex, relativeLuminance` are available, imported from `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` (session-color.ts:2).
plan_corrections.correction: No change needed. All four exist and are exported from `packages/utils/src/color.ts` at lines 320, 392, 423, 471. Note for the implementer: `loader.ts:3` imports `adjustHsv` from the SUBPATH `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/color`, not the barrel — keep new color imports on the subpath to match. `oklchToHex` gamut-maps by chroma bisection and clamps, so it always returns valid 6-digit hex and never needs a post-check.
plan_corrections.evidence: `git grep -n 'export function hexToOklch|export function oklchCusp|export function oklchToHex|export function relativeLuminance' -- packages/utils/src` → color.ts:320, :392, :423, :471. `sed -n '3p' packages/tui/src/theme/loader.ts` → `import { adjustHsv } from "@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/color";`.

plan_corrections.claim: Tests live at `packages/tui/test/*.test.ts`; tui has 221 test files.
plan_corrections.correction: Convention holds and matters: `find packages/tui/src -name '*.test.ts' | wc -l` returns 0, confirming nothing is colocated. A new `*.test.ts` under `packages/tui/src/` would never be run. The count drifted from 221 to 222 since the plan was written; use the count only as a sanity check, never as an acceptance number.
plan_corrections.evidence: `find packages/tui -name '*.test.ts' -not -path '*/node_modules/*' | wc -l` → 222. `find packages/tui/src -name '*.test.ts' | wc -l` → 0. Existing neighbors to read first: `packages/tui/test/settings-list-theme.test.ts` (uses `initTheme()` in `beforeAll`), `theme-color-mode.test.ts`, `theme-auto-detection.test.ts`.

open_questions: S or M? The plan insists this be decided before planning and warns against defaulting to the cheap version, on the grounds that the cheap version does not equal the reference's two hand-tuned themes. My recommendation is the opposite, for a specific reason: the plan's stated justification for M was the 99-palette audit, and that audit is now done and clean (see plan_corrections #2). M's remaining benefit is design PARITY with CCB, not correctness — and M buys that parity with a harness that then only checks 2 hand-picked themes, a strictly weaker regression net than the S variant's 101. Ship S now; file M as design follow-up. If a human still wants parity, the honest scope is two new JSON files in `defaults/` plus a designer pass plus an accessibility review — not a code change.

Exact target hues. The code_shape below proposes blue ~250 for the green family, magenta ~350 for error, amber ~80 for dirty-git. Those are my estimates, not measured. Before shipping, someone who is actually red-green colorblind should confirm 250/350/80 are distinguishable to them, and confirm the two amber/orange dirty-git bands that the audit found (orange, amber, gold, bronze, coral, ember variants) still read as 'warning' and not as 'error' at 350.

Should `statusLineGitDirty` change at all? Under pure deuteranopia the load-bearing confusion is red vs green. Once green becomes blue, red stays distinguishable, so dirty-git (amber) arguably needs no remap. I remap it anyway so it is separated from error by hue, but a human should confirm that is an improvement and not just a second change.

Contrast threshold. The repo's only existing constant is `ACCENT_MIN_CONTRAST = 3` (session-color.ts:36, WCAG AA large text). The status line is small text, so AA body (4.5:1) is the defensible gate. Confirm — 4.5 may make some of the 101 existing themes red on day one, which turns a feature PR into a 101-palette remediation project.

notes: `resolvedColors` is typed `Record<keyof T, string | number>` from `resolveThemeColors`, so indexing it with a plain string key will not typecheck as-is. If TS complains, widen to a `Record<string, string | number>` local view of it rather than casting to `any` -- AGENTS.md forbids `any`.

`adjustHsv` (the current transform) is HSV and non-perceptual: it shifts saturation by a fixed factor and ignores gamut, so a saturated source can clip. The OKLCH path carries L and C into a gamut-checked target, which is why the existing `COLORBLIND_ADJUSTMENT = { h: 60, s: 0.71 }` is deleted rather than reused.
Do NOT put a hue table in `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/*.kdl`. AGENTS.md scopes that tree to MODEL and PROVIDER policy, not TUI theme colors. There is no `gen:compat` step for this file.

Then `bun test packages/tui/test/daltonized-theme.test.ts packages/tui/test/theme-contrast-harness.test.ts` -- which will report 0 pass / 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64' until the addon is built. Confirm the failure is the addon and not an assertion, by checking the error text.

test_contract:
Three contracts, each with a named observable failure.

(1) POSITIVE COVERAGE. With colorBlindMode on, all five tokens in DALTONIZE_TARGET_HUE differ from their colorBlindMode-off values. Consumer-visible failure: a red-green colorblind user enables Color-Blind Mode, the success tick and the clean-git indicator stay green, and they read a successful tool call as an added diff line -- the exact misread this setting is supposed to prevent. Assert by building a Theme from a known palette both ways and comparing the five token values, not by asserting the literal output hex (the hues are a human decision, per open_questions, so pinning them would make every future tweak a test edit).

(2) EVERY OUTPUT IS A VALID HEX. After createTheme with colorBlindMode on, each of the five tokens matches /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i, for all 101 builtin themes. Consumer-visible failure: a theme throws inside Bun.color at render time, or the TUI emits a broken SGR sequence and the diff view corrupts. This is the check that would have caught a number or empty-string value sneaking through the remap -- today guarded only by startsWith("#").

(3) NEGATIVE IDENTITY -- the strongest and cheapest. With colorBlindMode omitted or false, every token of every builtin theme is byte-identical to the value before this change. Consumer-visible failure: a user who never enabled Color-Blind Mode gets a silently different UI after an upgrade. This is the contract that makes the change safe to ship, and it is what pins the branch to 'only when the flag is set'.

(4) CONTRAST, across all 101 builtin themes, for the five pairs listed in step 7. Consumer-visible failure: after enabling the mode, the dirty-git indicator becomes unreadable against the status-line background in some theme. This is the only test that generalizes past the five tokens -- it is the regression net the 101-palette sweep exists to provide.

Per AGENTS.md: no `mock.module()`, no `mock.*` at all, no source-grep of any .ts file, no `expect(true).toBe(true)`, no bare `not.toThrow()`, no non-empty-string assertions. If the two files get folded into one, keep these four assertions distinct -- they defend different regressions.

Baseline confirmed at HEAD 808b365: `bun run check:ts` passes (all 15 packages Done, pi-tui 6.67s). `bun test` is BLOCKED in this environment -- the native addon is not built, so it reports `0 pass / 1 fail / 1 error` with 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64'. Build the addon before trusting any `bun test` result; a red run is not evidence of a real failure until that is resolved.
gate:
Three gates, all able to fail.

G1 (can fail): `bun run check:ts` exits non-zero if the DALTONIZE_TARGET_HUE indexing of `resolvedColors` does not typecheck, or if the new module violates the no-`any` / top-level-import rules. It was green at baseline, so a red is attributable to this change.

G2 (can fail): the contrast-4.5 harness goes red if any of the 101 builtin themes has a remapped token that fails its paired-background ratio. This gate is expected to be the expensive one -- it will likely surface themes that were already marginal before this change, and those become the remediation list rather than a reason to lower the threshold silently.

G3 (can fail, and is the one that matters): the negative-identity test goes red if the colorBlindMode branch is moved above `resolveThemeColors` (which would apply the remap to unresolved `$var` strings and change every theme regardless of the flag), if the branch is widened to a path that runs when the flag is false, or if the remap mutates shared state that leaks into the flag-off theme. All three are easy mistakes and all three are invisible in review.

A gate that cannot fail would be 'the file exists' or '99 palettes were iterated' -- neither proves the remap happened or that the flag still gates it.
